nom: PanOxyl Acne Foaming Wash with 10% Benzoyl Peroxide

segments.oily: Reviewers with oily skin say the wash leaves their face clean and smooth and reduces overall oiliness without making their skin produce more oil.
segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin are split: several say it dries their face out badly enough that they stopped using it there or limited it to problem spots, while at least one with dry skin reports no dryness issues at all.
segments.combination: Combination-skin reviewers generally recommend it for the acne-prone, oilier areas of the face but say the drier areas or cheeks can get tight and dry if it's used too often.
segments.sensitive: Reviewers with sensitive skin are advised, or advise others, to use it less than daily since it can irritate or dry sensitive skin, though a few, including one with eczema-prone sensitive skin, report no irritation at all.
segments.mature: A reviewer navigating perimenopausal hormonal breakouts reports the wash cleared cystic acne on her jawline, chin, and neck within a few weeks.

concerns.dehydration: Dryness is the most frequently reported side effect: many reviewers, especially with daily or twice-daily use, say it leaves their skin or specific areas such as nose creases or cheeks tight and dry enough to need a heavy moisturizer afterward, and a few with dry or sensitive skin stopped using it on their face for this reason; roughly as many others, including some with oily or combination skin, report no dryness at all and call it non-stripping.
concerns.redness: Several reviewers report the wash itself triggers redness, swelling, or a burning, sunburn-like reaction, in one case severe enough to require steroids and occurring even in someone who doesn't consider herself especially sensitive, typically tied to leaving it on too long or using it too often; others say it calms the look of inflamed, angry breakouts rather than causing redness.
concerns.spots: Several reviewers report a gradual fading of old acne scars and dark spots with continued use over months, though one notes she still has visible scars and dark spots she is continuing to work on even after the acne itself improved.
concerns.blemishes: The great majority of reviewers report clearer skin and fewer breakouts, including several with cystic, hormonal, or body acne who call it their most effective product, though many describe an initial 'purging' period of worse breakouts before improvement; a handful say it did nothing, stopped working after months or years of use, or made their breakouts dramatically worse.
concerns.oiliness: Reviewers with oily or combination skin report a visible reduction in facial oiliness with regular use, alongside clearer skin, without the product making their skin produce more oil.

aspects.libelle: Doesn't foam much despite the name

extraits.texte: Had a really bad allergic reaction to this, buyer please beware- im not even a super sensitive person but after using this the next morning i had to take steroids eyes were swollen shut, redness and swelling on my face and inner elbows, such a horrible experience
Not for dry skin. The cleanse is ok but dried my face out really bad
I like this product. I have eczema prone skin (sensitive) and it doesn't irritate my skin. It dries out my active acne as well and prevents new ones.

I highly recommend this face wash for hormonal acne. Peri menopause came with breakouts, and this face wash helped clear up my skin in a few weeks. I had cystic acne on my jawline, chin and neck. I highly recommend.

I give this 5 starts for performance, but 4.5 on advertisement because it doesn't foam. I used this acne face wash during an active break out and after only 2 washes my face is less inflamed and the acne has shrunk tremendously. I have combination oily skin and this did not irritate my skin or make my skin produce extra oil.

i used to have terrible back acne for YEARS (15 years) until i visted my dermatologist who recommended this for it. he said begin with 4% and then increase if necessary, so i started with the lowest percentage once a day, sometimes twice if i showered again. i also used it on my face, careful not to apply it to my eyes (come on y'all, it says to avoid eyes on the packaging lol) and after a couple of months i had no recurring acne! i noticed a difference within a few weeks but i noticed the biggest difference when i wasnt breaking out at ALL. i still have some hyper pigmentation, but he said to get rid of that you have to get rid of the acne and eventually the scars would fade :)) its been 10 months and the scars have faded, theyre still noticable but im no longer insecure about it. years ago, i would've given anything to be at this point, so i appreciate how far i've come. i stopped using it on my face because it was drying out my skin, but a couple of weeks of hyaluronic acid and moisturizer fixed it! i still use it on my face when im breaking out, but not as frequent as on my back (still daily!) if you're hesitant, just give it a shot and make aure youre religiously mousturizing and avoiding your eyes. its an acne wash, NOT A MAKEUP REMOVER lol

When I'm dealing with inflamed breakouts, especially those painful pimples or pustules under the skin, PanOxyl Face Wash 10% is one of those products I always end up coming back to. It's the kind of cleanser I know I can rely on when my skin starts acting up, it really helps calm things down and makes active breakouts look less angry much faster. The formula uses 10% benzoyl peroxide designed to target acne-causing bacteria and help keep pores clear. [Ps. It can bleach towels]. I have combination skin, so my only real complaint is that if I use it too often, it can dry out my cheeks, especially since that area is less oily for me. But as long as I follow with a good serum and moisturizer, it's still one of those cleansers I trust whenever I'm going through an inflammatory acne flare.
